front.title: AI Safety for AI-Assisted Cyberattacks: Defender-Side Execution Finality at the Protected Consequence Boundary

abstract.t:
Autonomous AI agents can now carry out parts of a cyber operation that previously needed repeated human effort: reconnaissance, tool selection, execution attempts, observation of results, and adaptation when a route fails. An attacker-controlled agent does not have to malfunction to be dangerous; it can follow malicious instructions efficiently, using stolen credentials and well-formed requests that existing controls accept as valid.
This document describes a defender-side architecture, called execution finality, that adds one bounded layer to existing security controls. An incoming request, credential, permitted API call, or agent-composed workflow does not by itself create authority for a sensitive consequence. The defender reconstructs the operation that would actually take effect, holds it in a non-effective state, evaluates authorization independently of the requester, and enforces the result at an enforcement point located at or immediately before the protected consequence. The document specifies placement rules, requirements, state handling, failure behavior, latency strategy, and test methods. It uses publicly reported AI-assisted activity against Taiwanese government agencies in 2026 as an illustrative threat scenario and does not claim that the architecture would have prevented that activity.
